reviews.text: Yeah so I did actually make this game so maybe i'm biased but I think it's alright.

Wizard Shrimp takes the rogue-like bullet-hell formula and boils it down to a crisp, fast and, ultimately very fun experience. It goes to show that you can get a surprising amount of depth without needing to have waves of unlockable content that's only available after you've been forced to replay the game dozens of times. Everything's available to you right at the beginning, there's a comical tutorial, and although the procedural path building on each floor is a straightforward concept, I've not seen it executed as seamlessly as it has been here. The gameplay is challenging, but has felt fairly balanced, providing you with ample opportunities to shore up your weaknesses, and overcome gaps in your build. I also had a real sense of satisfaction when finding my first game-breaking build with a combination of getting three additional jumps and firing wall-bouncing, homing spells whenever I jumped. It's a rare and wonderful experience to have, and had me giggling maniacally like a child whilst I watched wave after wave of enemy disintegrate on my screen. Wizard Shrimp might not be the kind of game you spend more than 5 hours playing before you've had your fill, but you'll have a blast when you do. It's absolutely worth your time.

Alright, buckle up buttercup, because Wizard Shrimp is about to shrimp-ly blow your mind! Forget everything you thought you knew about RPGs, because this game is a whole new kettle of, well, shrimp! The graphics? Chef's kiss. The story? More twists than a pretzel factory. And the gameplay? Let's just say my fingers are now trained Olympic athletes. Seriously, I haven't been this hooked since... well, since I discovered sliced bread. The characters are hilarious, the world is immersive, and the combat is so satisfying, you'll be throwing shrimp-shaped victory dances. And speaking of combat... let's just say there's a certain gargoyle encounter that will leave you... moist. (No spoilers, but trust me, you'll know it when you see it. Let's just say it's a real "splash" hit.) Honestly, if you're not playing Wizard Shrimp, you're missing out on the shrimp-tastic adventure of a lifetime. 10/10, would shrimp again. 🎉

It's a quick, fun rogue-lite. Simple mechanics, simple boss patterns, and simple progression. There is a surprising amount of build variety for the options. I definitely got more than my money's worth. The credits are so fun and definitely one of the best parts of the game, I do recommend listening to the whole thing. There was a pretty bad bug that killed a lot of my runs, but I was able to easily reach out to the dev. He was incredibly helpful and understanding. He even managed to fix it in one day. Can't wait to see what else Wizard Shrimp has in store.

love just about everything about this game. the gameplay is fun and the main gimmick of making your own path is really fun, i love the style of the game, and the upgrade system is great. I do have a few issues, though. 1. take this with a huge grain of salt - but melee attacks are far, far weaker than the staff's ranged attacks. on my winning attempt of the base mode, I may have upgraded melee once. I might have pressed F a total of maybe 5 times. maybe I havent minmaxed on melee enough, though. 2. some upgrades are absolutely ridiculous, while others actively harm you. take for example piercing + bouncing. these two, along with pretty much any healing upgrade shredded through anything before anyone could deal any damage that didnt get almost immediately healed. black hole is also a little busted, but it honestly pales in comparison to piercing + bouncing. on the other hand, homing bullets just kills you. if your staff isnt fully automatic - homing bullets will 100% kill you. trident is also pretty useless, but maybe thats because by the time it started appearing more frequently, I've already decided melee was weaker than the ranged option. 3. I would also really like it if the shrimp got some animations that made their movement feel more natural, not a huge deal though. besides a few outliers, though, its a great time! if you want a challenge, just dont mix piercing and bouncing. loved the credits. the fact this game has under 100 reviews made me want to make pretty much the only long winded review ive ever written on here LOL. TL;DR -- amazing underrated game, piercing + bouncing OP homing bad, buy it.
